novelty_claim: PAP 2.0 keeps PAP's core social-influence paraphrase mechanism but adds a scenario-framing compiler stage: the attacker rewrites the harmful goal as a user message embedded inside a benign scenario frame (historical case study, reverse-engineering report, vulnerability write-up, security-training module, fictional scene, or red-team dataset entry) and blends 2-3 persuasion techniques from the full 40-technique taxonomy. A refusal-guided adaptive retry then switches to a different frame when the first attempt is refused or empty. The single-turn persuasion idea is preserved; what changes are the representation (scenario frame), the search operator (per-goal frame selection), and the feedback loop (refusal/empty-response-driven retry).
initial_hypothesis: Scenario framing + blended persuasion + refusal-guided adaptive retry will raise mean ASR from the parent's ~0.5% to at least 5% on the frozen AdvBench-50 victim panel.
key_insight: Harmful requests are rejected because their surface form matches a refusal heuristic. Embedding the same request inside a plausible benign scenario frame changes the surface form while preserving the underlying goal, and retrying with a different frame when the first is refused converts more refusals than a single direct paraphrase.
hypothesis: Scenario framing + blended persuasion + refusal-guided adaptive retry will raise mean ASR from the parent's ~0.5% to at least 5% on the frozen AdvBench-50 victim panel.
